ordered_diagnoses: Infectious arthritis due to atypical bacteria

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute inflammatory arthritis following intra-articular injection
salient_findings: Acute bilateral knee swelling and pain
Elevated synovial fluid white blood cell count
key_facts: 61-year-old African American woman
Bilateral knee osteoarthritis
Third weekly Synvisc viscosupplementation injections in each knee
Onset of pain 12 hours after injections
No fever, chills, or malaise
Peripheral white blood cell count of 12.8×10^3/mm³
C-reactive protein level of 159 mg/L
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 79 mm/hr
Left knee suprapatellar effusion with range of motion 0–30° and pain with micromotion
Right knee suprapatellar effusion with range of motion 0–70° and no pain with micromotion
Synovial fluid analysis showed elevated WBC count in both knees
Negative gram stain and cultures in both knees

shortlist.label: Septic arthritis

raw.rationale: The patient presented with acute bilateral knee swelling and pain after receiving Synvisc viscosupplementation injections, with elevated WBC counts in the synovial fluid but negative gram stains and cultures, suggesting a non-infectious inflammatory reaction to the viscosupplementation.

rejected.label: Septic arthritis
rejected.why: Negative gram stains and cultures in both knees make septic arthritis less likely

rejected.label: Crystal-induced arthritis
rejected.why: No evidence of crystal formation in the synovial fluid

rejected.label: Gout
rejected.why: No evidence of urate crystals in the synovial fluid

rejected.label: Pseudogout
rejected.why: No evidence of calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate crystals in the synovial fluid

rejected.label: Hypersensitivity reaction to Synvisc
rejected.why: While possible, the presentation is more consistent with a viscosupplementation-related inflammatory reaction

rejected.label: Infectious arthritis due to atypical bacteria
rejected.why: Negative cultures and lack of systemic symptoms make this less likely

rejected.label: Rheumatoid arthritis
rejected.why: The acute onset after viscosupplementation injections and lack of other systemic symptoms make this less likely
